Definition: properly, dark (as enveloped), i.e. the north; hence (by orientation), the left hand
BiblicalUsage: Semo'wl is the left hand, the north by orientation, and it places men and things. The sons of Merari stood on the left hand in the service of the house, and Solomon put five bases on the right side of the house and five on the left, with the sea on the right side eastward over against the south.
TheologicalSignificance: What I see here is that the left has its appointed place as surely as the right — Merari's sons stood there, and the bases stood there, by design.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
